successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Bulungan, the eastern shores of North Kalimantan toward Tawau, 'completely incorporated ... into the Dutch East Indies in June 1878'

rulers.name: Datuk Alam (Sultan Khalifatul Alam Muhammad Adil)

ledger.x: 1731: Wira Amir, newly Muslim as Sultan Amiril Mukminin, founds the sultanate.
1731: the new sultanate stands under Berau.
1731: the capital moves from Busang Arau to Salim Batu ('Wira Amir moved his capital from Busang Arau to Salim Batu'; the capital table has Limbu 1695-1731).
1777: Sultan Alimuddin moves the capital to Tanjung Palas ('Aji Ali succeeded his father as Sultan Alimuddin and moved the capital from Salim Batu to Tanjung Palas').
1789: Bulungan passes under Sulu's overlordship after Sulu sacks Berau.
1789: Bulungan 'declared independence from Berau' after Sulu sacked Berau (page; infobox ends the vassalage in 1789).
27 September 1834: Bulungan becomes a Dutch protectorate.

1855: 'Bulungan stopped paying tribute to Sulu for 50 years, thereby becoming de facto independent from Sulu' (infobox: Sulu vassalage 1789-1855; the page adds that the influence 'officially ended in 1878').
June 1878: the protectorate (infobox 1834-1878) ends in annexation; 'Bulungan was finally incorporated into the colonial empire of the Dutch East Indies in June 1878'.

wars.name: Bulungan's war with the Tidungs and the Sebuku villages
wars.outcome: Bulungan 'subjugated' the Tidungs and the Sebuku villages in 1849 and its jurisdiction reached toward Tawau.

certainty.note: Forest and river frontiers with the Tidung Lands, Berau and the Apo Kayan interior; the 1913/1915 British-Dutch border agreements come after this dossier ends.
